dod_intent_evidence: GLADIUS acoustic c-UAS system completed a DIU-hosted Technology Demonstration sponsored by CENTCOM (April 2026, 100% sUAS detection across 4 Critical Operational Issues) and was tested with DIU/CENTCOM in an Army Transformation in Contact exercise — homepage News section.
score_evidence: 'achieving a 100% detection rate of sUAS flights' is the closest thing to a lab-brag stat, but it's wrapped in operational test language (COIs), not accuracy-for-its-own-sake → lab_language_intensity kept low

site uses genuine operational-test vocabulary — 'Critical Operational Issues — Performance Effectiveness, Suitability, Mission Impact, and Maintainability' and 'operationally relevant environment' → deployment_awareness_absence kept low

'Warfighters first... empower humans, who will always be more important than hardware, with solutions that sharpen edge lethality without increasing cognitive burden' and founders who personally commanded Joint & Special Operations Forces → operator_absence very low

founding hires were 'Founding Electro-Mechanical Engineer' (move from prototypes to manufacturing) and 'Founding ML Engineer' (hardware that 'succeeds in the mud'); live Blitz roles are Staff Mechatronics/Robotics Engineer — deployment/manufacturing-skewed hiring → hiring_profile_skew kept low
pre-seed, 3-5 employees, founded 2025, prototype status, single successful demo event with no visible follow-on program of record yet → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: 100% sUAS detection rate comes from one DIU/CENTCOM Technology Demonstration, not sustained contested-noise operation
blind_spots.operator_reality: A real battlefield has gunfire, vehicle engines, artillery, wind, and multiple simultaneous acoustic sources — an acoustic sensor validated in a single scheduled demo event has not yet proven it holds up to the acoustic clutter of an actual firefight, which is a fundamentally different signal environment
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: the news item reports the COI results and detection rate but never addresses acoustic environment complexity or false-alarm rate under battlefield noise
blind_spots.evidence_quote: achieving a 100% detection rate of sUAS flights

blind_spots.blind_spot: Claims integrated alerting 'across existing awareness kits' without naming ATAK/TAK
blind_spots.operator_reality: If GLADIUS pushes alerts into the situational-awareness ecosystem soldiers actually carry, that's almost certainly ATAK/TAK — not naming it either means the integration is thinner than claimed or the messaging hasn't caught up to what acquisition officers will ask for by name
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: site describes the alerting UX benefit (low cognitive load) without the specific integration standard
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Integrated alerting moves at digital speed across existing awareness kits, all without increasing cognitive load

blind_spots.blind_spot: No battery, spares, or power-logistics detail for a soldier-worn dismounted device
blind_spots.operator_reality: 'Dismounted' means a soldier is carrying and powering this in the field for extended patrols — battery life, charging/spares logistics, and GFE power integration determine whether it's actually usable past the first mission, and none of that is addressed
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: site markets the device as 'Lightweight' and 'portable' but never quantifies battery life, weight, or field sustainment plan
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Ground-based Lightweight Acoustic Dismounted Integrated UAS Sensor (GLADIUS)

opener_hook: GLADIUS hit 100% sUAS detection in the April 2026 DIU/CENTCOM demo — was that in a quiet range or amid real acoustic clutter?
what_they_do: Pre-seed TurbineOne spinout building GLADIUS, a soldier-worn acoustic sensor that detects approaching drones and pushes real-time alerts, founded by military veterans and already demoed with DIU/CENTCOM.
